candidates.old:
LDX #&02
    STX movers_to_update_count
    LDY movers_to_update_base
    LDA movers_raster_y,Y
    STA movers_to_update_raster_y + 2
    STY movers_to_update + 2
    LDX um_next - 1,Y
    LDA movers_raster_y,X
    STA movers_to_update_raster_y + 1
    STX movers_to_update + 1
    LDY um_next - 1,X
    LDA movers_raster_y,Y
    STA movers_to_update_raster_y
    STY movers_to_update
    LDX um_next - 1,Y
    STX movers_to_update_base
.update_movers_loop
    LDX #&02                        \ grind: the last slot holding the lowest raster y, as the
    LDA movers_to_update_raster_y + 1 \ original's search found it (a later slot wins a tie)
    CMP movers_to_update_raster_y + 2
    BCS find_topmost_check_slot_0   \ slot 1 >= slot 2: slot 2 stays
    DEX                             \ slot 1 < slot 2: slot 1
.find_topmost_check_slot_0
    LDA movers_to_update_raster_y
    CMP movers_to_update_raster_y,X
    BCS found_topmost_mover         \ slot 0 >= the candidate: the candidate stays
    LDX #&00
.found_topmost_mover
    LDA #&FF
    STA movers_to_update_raster_y,X \ Set to maximum value to prevent being found again
    LDY movers_to_update,X
    STY mover_to_update
    JSR update_mover                \ Update mover
    DEC movers_to_update_count
    BPL update_movers_loop
candidates.new:
\ grind: the chain's three movers go to the slots in processing order, their raster ys sorted as they
    \ stand now (stable: a tie keeps the chain order, as the search for the topmost one, a later slot
    \ winning a tie, found it). Slot 0 is movers_to_update_count (&C1: the loop counter is gone with the
    \ loop; read before any update_mover). The raster y copies and the FF marks go too: nothing else reads
    \ them. In order is the usual case: two compares, nothing moved.
    LDY movers_to_update_base
    STY movers_to_update_count      \ slot 0 = the base
    LDX um_next - 1,Y
    STX movers_to_update + 1        \ slot 1 = the next
    LDY um_next - 1,X
    STY movers_to_update + 2        \ slot 2 = the next after
    LDA um_next - 1,Y
    STA movers_to_update_base
.umsort_loop                        \ X = slot 1's mover, Y = slot 2's
    LDA movers_raster_y,Y
    CMP movers_raster_y,X
    BCS umsort_slot_0               \ slot 2 >= slot 1: in order
    STY movers_to_update + 1        \ exchange slots 1 and 2
    STX movers_to_update + 2
    LDX movers_to_update + 1        \ X = slot 1's mover again
.umsort_slot_0
    LDY movers_to_update_count
    LDA movers_raster_y,X
    CMP movers_raster_y,Y
    BCS umsort_done                 \ slot 1 >= slot 0: in order (Y = slot 0's mover)
    STX movers_to_update_count      \ exchange slots 0 and 1, then slots 1 and 2 again
    STY movers_to_update + 1
    LDX movers_to_update + 1
    LDY movers_to_update + 2
    BRA umsort_loop
.umsort_done
    STY mover_to_update             \ slot 0 (Y)
    JSR update_mover                \ Update mover
    LDY movers_to_update + 1
    STY mover_to_update
    JSR update_mover
    LDY movers_to_update + 2
    STY mover_to_update
    JSR update_mover
candidates.summary: Replace update_movers' populate-and-search (three raster y copies, then three restarting searches with FF marks, 215.8 cycles a pass) with a stable sort of the chain's three movers' ids by raster y (two compares when already in order, a bubble pass or two otherwise) followed by three straight update_mover calls. Slot 0 of the ids reuses the dead loop counter movers_to_update_count (&C1). The order is exactly the original's (ascending raster y, a tie going to the earlier of base, next, next after: the old search let the higher slot win a tie, and slot 2 was the base). Measured (pcprof, bench build, 2026-10-22): logic 8634 -> 8525 a pass on seed 1, 10255 -> 10139 holding RIGHT; state and screen identical to the control over 6000 passes of seed 1 and 6000 of seed 3 (the swap paths run in 28% and 35% of passes). Same size (82 bytes), so nothing after it moves.
candidates.equivalence: The old code took the three movers of the chain (base b, next n, next after c; the base advanced to the one after c), copied their raster ys, then three times picked the slot with the lowest copied raster y (a later slot winning a tie: slot 2 = b, 1 = n, 0 = c), marked it FF, and called update_mover on it. The pick order is therefore the stable ascending sort of [b, n, c] by raster y (ties keep the chain order); the copies are a snapshot taken before any update_mover, and so are the compares of the new code, all done before the first call. Raster ys are result_high of times_78 (at most &4D, written only at movers_raster_y,Y in the mover update), so never equal to the FF marker and no marked slot could be re-picked in the old code. The new code stores b, n, c to slot 0, 1, 2, advances the base exactly as before (um_next chain, stored before any call), then runs a bubble sort with strict-less swaps: cs(1,2) (swap if r(slot 2) < r(slot 1)), cs(0,1) (swap if r(slot 1) < r(slot 0), and then back to cs(1,2)), exit when cs(0,1) does not swap straight after cs(1,2). Adjacent strict swaps are stable; the loop ends with slot 0 <= slot 1 <= slot 2 and every pass of it strictly reduces the inversions, so it terminates in at most 3 trips. Register state at each label: umsort_loop X = id of slot 1, Y = id of slot 2 (from populate; from the swap-back, reloaded from the slots); umsort_slot_0 X = id of slot 1 (swap path: reloaded after the exchange); at umsort_done Y = id of slot 0 (set by LDY just before the BCS). Then update_mover is called with Y = mover id and mover_to_update = Y, in slot order, as before (liveness: only Y is live into it). Nothing else reads movers_to_update_raster_y, the old FF marks, movers_to_update (the slots are written before they are read) or movers_to_update_count (&C1: text_offset in the front end only, written before it is read there; in play it was only this loop's counter, left at &FF after the loop and read by nothing); movers_to_update_base is written to the same value at the same point in the routine. Flags, A, X, Y after the last JSR are dead (the next code is LDA helicopter_to_update).
candidates.relies_on: Same size as the window (82 bytes, ASSERTed by the listing: update_movers_loop's successor wait_for_timer_281a stays at &2456 in the bench build, so no code or table after the window moves and no page crossing outside it changes). Inside the window every branch stays in page &24 (BCS umsort_slot_0 &2413 -> &241E, BCS umsort_done &2426 -> &2435, BRA umsort_loop &2433 -> &240D); movers_raster_y,X/Y (&13EE + 1..9) and um_next - 1,X/Y (&23EE + 1..9, ASSERTed same page) cross no page. Relies on: raster ys being below &80 (in fact at most &4D) and on nothing but this routine reading movers_to_update, movers_to_update_raster_y (now unused, left declared outside the window), or &C1 between update_movers' start and the next write. update_mover and what it calls leave &C1 alone (the old loop kept its counter there across them) but the new code no longer needs it to survive a call: slot 0 is read before the first JSR. um_next is in moved_0a20 in GAMEPLAY builds: the window is the same there. Uses the 65C02 opcode set (BRA only; PHY/PLX not needed).
